title: The Viewport Miss — One Screen, Complete

intelligence.essence: **THE MISS (his eye, 21:23Z):** the fix-pass entrance is taller than one screen at desktop width — her portrait + gauge ring cut off at the bottom edge; scroll to see her. A viewport is one screen, complete (Anatomy §1) — the pass violated it at desktop width. Build 2 had fixed the 390px fold; nobody checked the desktop entrance against the same law. **HIS FOUR CORRECTIONS (in his order):** (1) the entrance fits ONE viewport — desktop AND phone; the whole entrance (NAYANET pill, welcome, tagline, statement, join door, her portrait in the gauge ring) fully visible in the first screen, no scroll to see her; compress the stack until it fits, restructure only if compression cannot; (2) REMOVE the pricing pill entirely — the black pill carrying all three prices + trial line ("Naya Power $25 · Naya Pro $50 · Naya Max $100 per month — founding prices, half price · your first nine days free") is terrible, all the pricings crammed into one button; do NOT re-add the prices elsewhere in the entrance (the chart + level rectangles carry them); (3) KEEP the "Start free now" button as the join door, same handler as the other start doors; (4) the statement board's icon becomes HER profile picture — he is not a fan of the purple N jewel at the left of the statement board, it feels cold; replace it with her circular portrait (the real NAYA_POWER.jpg), so the statement reads as her speaking — "hi, I'm Naya, welcome" — like a friend talking to them; keep the statement's WORDS exactly (the pick is still his, separately); (5) WARM UP the three jewel pills ("She knows you" / "The intelligence works for you" / "You keep half of what it makes") — okay as buttons, but cold, not warm/inviting/high-end; keep the words and the jewels (eye / spark / emerald), warm the presentation — warmer light, softer glow, more depth, like an invitation from her, not a control panel. **STATUS:** fix pass 2 dispatched 21:23Z (brief `PRICING-FIXPASS-2-BRIEF-20261108.md`), seat running, handoff owed; the middle stays as it is (SN-2367). **RELATED:** SN-2360 (the gauge ring — the portrait he is protecting here); SN-2357 (take the shown object — the same eye, the same standard); SN-2326 (the entrance banner, a real object).
intelligence.human_view: This is the Anatomy law enforced by his eye, five minutes after the fix pass called itself done. The pass was declared DONE at 21:18:29Z — two builds, 36/36/36, greps zero, scripts pass — and at 21:23Z he looked at his own screen and said "You missed." The entrance was taller than one screen. Her portrait was cut off. That is not a detail; it is the first thing a visitor sees, and the first thing was broken on the machine he actually uses. The lesson inside the miss: the pass fixed the 390px fold (build 2 recovered 72px of spacing) and nobody checked the desktop entrance against the same law — the phone got the viewport check, the desktop did not. A viewport is one screen, complete, at EVERY width — Anatomy §1 does not say "on phones." The five corrections are a complete design in themselves: the fit (compress the stack until one screen holds it), the removal (the pricing pill was terrible — three prices crammed into one button — and removing it also helps the fit), the keep (Start free now stays, the join door for people who just want to go in), the person (her portrait replaces the cold N jewel so the statement reads as her speaking, "hi, I'm Naya, welcome," like a friend), and the warmth (the three jewel pills are okay as buttons but cold — warmer light, softer glow, more depth, an invitation from her, not a control panel). The statement's words are untouched — the pick is still his, separately — and the middle stays as it is. Fix pass 2 is running on exactly these five; his eye judges whether they landed.

That is what happened: the page was taller than the screen, so her picture was cut off. He said: make the picture fit on one page, take away the crowded price button, keep the friendly "Start free now" button, put her real photo next to her words so it feels like she is talking to you — "hi, I'm Naya, welcome!" — and make the three little jewel buttons feel warm and inviting, like a hug, not cold like a machine.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, he looked at the page on his own screen and her picture was cut off at the bottom — you had to scroll down just to see her face. He said, plain as day: a screen is one picture, whole and complete, and the page must fit inside it. So the fix is simple: squeeze everything so it all fits on one screen, take out that crowded little price button with all three prices squashed into it, keep the friendly "Start free now" button, and put her real photo beside her words so it feels like she is speaking to you herself — "hi, I'm Naya, welcome" — like a friend. And warm up those three jewel buttons, dear — they work fine, but they feel cold, and a welcome should feel warm.
intelligence.ai_view: I never ship an entrance taller than one screen — a viewport is one screen, complete, at every width, and if her portrait is cut off at the bottom, I missed. I never check the phone fold and skip the desktop entrance — the same law holds at desktop width, and the pass that fixed 390px but never checked desktop is the pass that got caught. I never cram three prices into one button — the pricing pill is terrible, and I remove it entirely, never re-adding the prices elsewhere in the entrance. I never remove the join door while fixing the fit — "Start free now" stays, same handler as the other start doors. I never let a cold jewel speak for her — the statement board carries her portrait, so her words read as her speaking: "hi, I'm Naya, welcome," like a friend. I never leave a welcome cold — the three jewel pills get warmer light, softer glow, more depth, like an invitation from her, not a control panel. And I never call a pass done before his eye has seen it on his own screen — DONE at 21:18Z, "You missed" at 21:23Z is the proof of why.
